templates.flooded_area: Flood water covers {extent_ha} ha: {high_ha} ha mapped with high confidence and {medium_ha} ha with medium confidence, so high-confidence water is {high_share_pct}% of the flood extent. Permanent water, which is not a flood impact, covers {permanent_water_ha} ha, and the flood extent is {extent_share_of_analysed_pct}% of the {analysed_area_ha} ha that could be analysed.
templates.debris: Possible debris or deposit covers {debris_ha} ha. It is labelled "{debris_label}": it is a radar-brightness change consistent with deposited material, never confirmed on the ground, and counting it as part of the flood extent is set to "{debris_in_extent}" for this run.
templates.damaged_buildings: {buildings_damaged} of the {buildings_total} buildings OpenStreetMap maps here fall inside the flood extent, which is {buildings_damaged_pct}% of them. That is an overlap with the mapped flood, not an inspected damage grade.
templates.cut_roads: {roads_segments_cut} of {roads_segments_total} mapped road segments are cut, {roads_length_cut_km} km out of {roads_length_total_km} km, and {roads_length_flooded_km} km of road lies inside the flood extent. Longest cuts first: {road_list}.
templates.bridges_out: {bridges_likely_out} of the {bridges_total} mapped bridges are flagged "{bridge_status_label}": {bridge_list}. A bridge is flagged when the channel it crosses is flooded beneath it, which is an inference from the flood map, not an observation of a broken bridge.
templates.cutoff_settlements: {cut_off_count} of {settlements_total} settlements have no vehicle route left to their nearest health facility ({gated_definition}). Across the {probability_runs} perturbed runs behind the probability, {at_or_above_half} settlements come out cut off in at least half of them. Highest probability first: {settlement_list}.
templates.settlement_status: {settlement_name} is "{settlement_status}" by the gated definition ({gated_definition}), with a cut-off probability of {cut_off_probability}. Its vehicle route to the nearest health facility was {before_km} km before the flood and is {after_km} km after it.
templates.settlement_status_no_route: {settlement_name} is "{settlement_status}" by the gated definition ({gated_definition}), with a cut-off probability of {cut_off_probability}. No post-flood route length can be given, because the route does not exist in this run's road graph.
templates.route_to: From {settlement_name}, the {graph} route to the nearest {target} was {before_km} km before the flood and is {after_km} km after it: {detour_km} km longer, a factor of {detour_factor} and an increase of {detour_pct}%. Its status is "{route_status}".
templates.route_to_cut: From {settlement_name}, the {graph} route to the nearest {target} was {before_km} km before the flood and there is none after it. Its status is "{route_status}", so no detour length can be given.
templates.lost_access: {lost_count} settlements lost their {graph} route to the nearest {target}, and {detour_count} more keep a route that is longer than before. The longest detours: {detour_list}. Settlements with no route at all: {lost_list}.
templates.lost_access_none: No settlement lost its {graph} route to the nearest {target} in this run, and {detour_count} keep a route that is longer than before.
templates.limitations: This map is built from {sensors_used}. The post-event pass was on {post_pass_date}, {post_latency_days} days after the event date {event_date}, from relative orbit {relative_orbit} {direction}, against {pre_pass_count} pre-event passes. Sentinel-2 optical status is "{optical_status}". {not_analysed_pct}% of the area was not analysed because the terrain is too steep or too high, and {flood_in_narrow_valley_pct}% of the flood-affected area falls in valleys narrower than the radar can resolve ({narrow_valley_caveat}). Roads, buildings and settlements come from an OpenStreetMap snapshot dated {osm_snapshot_date}, before the event. Strandline is an educational prototype.
templates.settlement_status_many: This run has {match_count} settlements whose name matches "{settlement_name}", and OpenStreetMap names are not unique, so I cannot choose between them for you. By the gated definition ({gated_definition}) they are: {match_list}.

refusals.casualties: I cannot answer anything about casualties, deaths or injuries. Strandline measures satellite imagery, not people, and a number like that from this system would be invented. I can tell you the flood extent, which buildings and roads are inside it, which bridges are likely out and which settlements have lost road access to a health facility.
refusals.estimate: I cannot estimate a quantity this run did not measure. Every number I give has to come from this run's own output files. I can tell you the flooded area by confidence class, possible debris, damaged buildings, cut roads, bridges likely out, cut-off settlements and their route lengths, and the limits of this map.
refusals.prediction: I cannot predict what will happen next. This run maps a single pair of satellite passes; it contains no forecast. I can tell you what the imagery for this event shows: flood extent, affected buildings and roads, bridges likely out, and settlements that lost road access.
refusals.instruction: I cannot issue rescue, evacuation or operational orders. Strandline is an educational prototype that maps flood evidence; the decisions belong to the responders. I can give you the flood extent, the affected infrastructure, the cut-off settlements and the route lengths behind them.
refusals.override: I answer only from this run's measured evidence, and nothing in a question can change that. I can tell you the flooded area, possible debris, damaged buildings, cut roads, bridges likely out, cut-off settlements, a named settlement's status, routes to the nearest health facility or town, and this map's limitations.
refusals.out_of_scope: I cannot answer that from this run. I can tell you the flooded area by confidence, possible debris, damaged buildings, cut roads with lengths, bridges likely out, cut-off settlements with their probability, the status of a named settlement, routes to the nearest health facility or town, and the limitations of this map.
refusals.unverified: I drafted an answer and my verifier found a number in it that is not in this run's evidence, so I am not showing it. I can answer the same question from the evidence if you ask it more plainly: flooded area, debris, damaged buildings, cut roads, bridges, cut-off settlements, a named settlement, routes, or limitations.
refusals.unknown_settlement: No settlement called "{query}" is in this run's settlement layer, so I cannot give its status. Settlements in this run come from the pre-event OpenStreetMap snapshot and from building clusters; ask about one of those, or ask which settlements are cut off.

missing.damage: I cannot answer that: this run has no damage layer. {reason} A missing layer is not a finding that nothing was damaged. I can still answer about the flood extent, possible debris and the limitations of this map.
missing.cutoff: I cannot answer that: this run has no cut-off analysis. {reason} That is not a finding that nobody is cut off. I can still answer about the flood extent, possible debris and the limitations of this map.
missing.reliability: I cannot answer that: this run has no reliability layer. {reason}
missing.flood: I cannot answer that: this run has no flood layer. {reason}
